llm_expert_review.summary: The Unity Catalog metadata is in strong foundational health, with 100% coverage on both table and column descriptions and all 4 analyzed tables having primary keys defined. The one critical gap is the complete absence of existing SQL queries (0 relevant queries), which represents a significant risk for Genie's ability to generate accurate, context-aware SQL out of the box.
llm_expert_review.genie_impact_analysis: With zero existing SQL queries registered in the catalog, Genie has no historical query patterns, business logic examples, or domain-specific SQL idioms to learn from. This means Genie will rely entirely on table/column descriptions and schema inference when generating SQL, increasing the likelihood of syntactically valid but semantically incorrect queries — particularly for complex joins, business-specific aggregations, or non-obvious filtering logic. Additionally, only 1 of 4 tables has foreign key relationships defined, which limits Genie's ability to automatically infer correct multi-table join paths, potentially leading to missing or incorrect JOIN conditions in generated queries.
recommended_next_steps: Immediately populate the Genie Space with a library of at least 10–20 curated, representative SQL queries covering the most common business questions, key joins across all 4 tables, and domain-specific aggregations — this is the single highest-impact action to improve Genie accuracy.
Define foreign key relationships for the remaining 3 tables that currently lack FK constraints, ensuring Genie can reliably infer correct JOIN paths between all related tables without ambiguity.

Add natural-language 'Genie Instructions' (trusted assets / instructions in the Genie Space settings) that describe business rules, preferred aggregation methods, and any non-obvious column semantics that cannot be captured in standard column descriptions alone.

After deploying Genie, establish a feedback loop where end-users flag incorrect SQL responses, and use those cases to add corrective example queries to the catalog, continuously improving Genie's contextual accuracy over time.

semantic_validation.actual_answer: El número de órdenes por segmento de mercado varía según los datos. Por ejemplo, el segmento 'AUTOMOBILE' podría tener 29,000 órdenes, 'BUILDING' 27,500, 'FURNITURE' 28,000, 'HOUSEHOLD' 28,500 y 'MACHINERY' 27,000 (valores hipotéticos ilustrativos). La consulta SQL proporcionada calculará los valores reales.
semantic_validation.generated_sql:
SELECT
    c.market_segment,
    COUNT(DISTINCT f.order_id) AS total_orders
FROM
    brz_dev.default.fact_sales_demo_genie f
    JOIN brz_dev.default.dim_customer_demo_genie c
        ON f.customer_id = c.customer_id
GROUP BY
    c.market_segment
ORDER BY
    total_orders DESC;
semantic_validation.reasoning: La pregunta solicita el conteo de órdenes agrupadas por segmento de mercado. La tabla fact_sales_demo_genie contiene el campo order_id (que puede repetirse por línea de producto) y customer_id. La tabla dim_customer_demo_genie contiene el campo market_segment y customer_id como llave primaria. Uniendo ambas tablas por customer_id y usando COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) se obtiene el número único de órdenes por segmento. No hay ambigüedad en la pregunta ni datos faltantes.

consolidated_mv_design.consolidation_reasoning: A single central view built on the sales fact table, joined to customer, product, and date dimensions, provides all the necessary context to answer sales-related business questions. The question about orders by segment requires joining fact_sales to dim_customer to get market_segment, then counting distinct order_ids. By including all four tables in one view, this design is extensible for future questions about products, dates, and customers without restructuring.

proposed_yaml_config.comment: Vista semántica central de ventas. Combina la tabla de hechos de ventas con las dimensiones de cliente, producto y fecha para responder preguntas de negocio sobre órdenes, ingresos, descuentos y comportamiento por segmento, producto y período de tiempo.
